findings.issue: The reuse identity is taken over the unjoined commands, so the left-out line (`left_out_line(name, path)`, printed from `identity["grading"]`) names the DECLARED entry, while the recorded step is now named for the joined step (`<entry> + affected/...`). The drive's `grades_left_out(text, s.get("name"))` matches the line by `startswith(form % name)` on the step's name, so for a joined step whose declared entry grades a left-out path it answers False and reports 'did not repeat ... <repeat_reason>' instead of the left-out reason. Only the explanation differs; the run itself is measured correctly (jn6 covers repeat_plan).
findings.resolution: Have `grades_left_out` match on `_evidence_io.step_parts(name)[0]` as well as the whole name, or print the left-out line under the step's joined name; add one drive case with a joined grading step.

findings.issue: The diff reserves a second step-name spelling (`<entry> + affected/<arm>: <suites>`), refusing it only at bind time (`_verdict_binding.gate_mismatch`, vb42). The write-time guards that refuse a gate entry starting with `DERIVED_STEP_PREFIX` were not widened, so a plan can carry such an entry and learns it cannot bind only when a commit is attempted. The executor named this as LEFT, but the class (a reader of a step name) is open on the write side of the same boundary.
findings.resolution: Use `_evidence_io.step_parts(entry) != (entry, [])` beside `is_derived_step` in `_manifest_rules.py:628` and `audit-task.py:15429`, with the message naming JOINED_STEP_SEPARATOR.
